To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the language generated by a context-free grammar is the same as the language generated by an equivalent simplified context-free grammar, where the simplified grammar has been produced by applying a combination of the four operations described in the paper.

(1) we formalized the fact that general CF grammars generate languages which are also generated by simpler CF grammars, (2) we formalized and proved the correctness of four simplification rules: useless symbol elimination, unreachable symbol elimination, unit rule elimination and empty rule elimination, (3) our formalization is written in Coq and can be downloaded from the web.

(1) useless symbol elimination preserves language generation; (2) inaccessible symbol elimination preserves language; generation; (3) unit rule elimination preserves language generation and (4) empty rule elimination preserves language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a proof of the fact that the language generated by a given context-free grammar is equal to the language generated by some simpler and equivalent contextfree grammar.
the formalization of the simplification operations on context-free grammars and the proofs of their correctness with respect to the generated languages.
the development of a proof of correctness for a set of operations that transform context-free grammars into equivalent grammars with less symbols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for any context-free grammar, there exists an equivalent context-free grammar with no useless symbols, no inaccessible symbols, no unit rules and no empty rules.
any context-free grammar can be reduced to an equivalent grammar with a smaller number of rules, and that this reduction process is correct.
the language generated by a given context-free grammar can be generated by another grammar that is equivalent to the first and is also simpler than the first.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formalized proofs of the correctness of the grammar simplification operations are a useful tool to verify and validate the correctness of the implementation of the grammar simplifier.
we have proved the correctness of the simplification of general context-free grammatical rules with respect to the generated language.
the Coq proof of the equivalence of two context-free grammars, which generate the same language, is possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formalization is a good way to check the correctness of the proofs and to find errors in the proofs.
it can be easily extended to include other operations such as useless nonterminals elimination and unreachable rules elimination.
the formalization of context-free grammar simplification operations is a useful and interesting task that can be performed using a proof assistant.
